programs.name: Anthropology
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: requirements are milestone-based (portfolio/position papers, oral qualifying exam, advancement to candidacy, teaching, and dissertation) with coursework set by subfield and advisor rather than a fixed university-published course worksheet; the MA is earned en route to the PhD, not as a terminal coursework degree. Concrete facts stated by the department: MA phase requires ANTH 230 Departmental Colloquium (4 quarters, 1 unit each), a ProSeminar (ANTH 281A/B/C), ANTH 295 Master's thesis preparation, four core seminars chosen from ANTH 280A-F (Social, Cultural, Psychological, Anthropological Archaeology, Biological, Linguistic; 4 units each), plus four letter-grade electives (4 units each, at least two within Anthropology), and an article-length master's paper (~5,000-10,000 words). The PhD adds two more letter-grade electives (12 letter-grade courses total), advancement to candidacy by roughly the 4th year (position papers ~50-60 pp, research proposal, oral qualifying exam, doctoral committee of >=4 UCSD faculty), possible foreign-language proficiency, at least one quarter as TA/Reader (ANTH 500), and a defended dissertation. Normative time is six to seven years. CPH is the doctoral candidate-in-philosophy status, not a separate coursework program.

programs.name: Anthropology and Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Interdisciplinary research doctorate (PhD in Anthropology and Cognitive Science): the home department is Anthropology and the degree is earned through the campus Interdisciplinary PhD Program (IDP) in Cognitive Science. Requirements are milestone-based, not a fixed course worksheet: a primary specialization completed through the Anthropology home department (good standing plus its candidacy requirements), a secondary specialization providing tools of inquiry in a second cognitive-science discipline, a breadth requirement of five classes spanning approaches across disciplines, qualifying examinations as specified by the home department demonstrating cross-disciplinary familiarity, and an interdisciplinary dissertation drawing on both specializations. The catalog notes the Anthropology/Cognitive Science pathway was under revision, so specific coursework is set by the department and IDP advisors rather than published as a fixed worksheet.

programs.name: Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Anthropology research doctorate (milestone-based, no fixed university-published course worksheet). The Anthropogeny specialization, administered with CARTA, adds to the base PhD: BIOM 225 (Introduction to Anthropogeny), BIOM 229 (Advanced Anthropogeny), and BIOM 218 (Current Topics in Anthropogeny, taken each quarter), plus monthly journal meetings and participation in CARTA symposia on human origins. The dissertation must be broadly related to human origins and interdisciplinary in nature. All base Anthropology PhD milestones (see AN75) still apply.

programs.name: Anthropology with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Anthropology research doctorate (milestone-based, no fixed university-published course worksheet). The Critical Gender Studies specialization adds: CGS 200 (Advanced Studies in Critical Gender Studies), CGS 299 (Practicum in Critical Gender Studies, during the final two years), three elective courses from a preapproved list, and at least one dissertation committee member from CGS faculty. All base Anthropology PhD milestones (see AN75) still apply.

programs.name: Anthropology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Anthropology research doctorate (milestone-based, no fixed university-published course worksheet). The Interdisciplinary Environmental Research specialization adds: SIO 295S-295LS (a 16-unit interdisciplinary summer boot camp), 8 units in a secondary field outside anthropology, SIO 296 (Interdisciplinary Environmental Research Forum, 6 units over 3 quarters), and a dissertation chapter of an interdisciplinary environmental nature. All base Anthropology PhD milestones (see AN75) still apply.

programs.name: Anthropology (Science Studies)
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Anthropology research doctorate (milestone-based, no fixed university-published course worksheet). The Science Studies specialization replaces some anthropology electives with the interdisciplinary Science Studies Program curriculum: a three-quarter core seminar sequence in the first year, a weekly colloquium (for course credit during the first two years), and an internship requirement (which may be waived for students with relevant prior experience). All base Anthropology PhD milestones (see AN75) still apply.

programs.name: Anthropology with a Specialization in Computational Social Science
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Anthropology research doctorate (milestone-based, no fixed university-published course worksheet). The Computational Social Science specialization adds: CSS 209 (Computational Social Science Research Seminar, three quarters), three elective courses (at least one outside the home department and at least one 'advanced data' course), at least one dissertation committee member from CSS-affiliated faculty, and a dissertation with a technical/computational component. All base Anthropology PhD milestones (see AN75) still apply.

programs.name: Anthropology with a Specialization in Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Anthropology research doctorate (milestone-based, no fixed university-published course worksheet). This is the Cognitive Science graduate specialization taken by Anthropology PhD students, coordinated with the Department of Cognitive Science; specific coursework and the breadth/qualifying requirements are set by the home department and Cognitive Science program rather than published as a fixed worksheet. Distinct administratively from the full interdisciplinary PhD in Anthropology and Cognitive Science (AN77). All base Anthropology PhD milestones (see AN75) still apply. Confidence is moderate because the exact overlay course list is not published in a single fixed catalog worksheet.

programs.name: Doctor of Audiology
programs.deptNotes: Joint doctoral program (SDSU + UC San Diego), clinical professional doctorate: requirements are milestone-based, not a fixed university-published course worksheet, so no course/unit table is provided. Concrete facts the official UCSD catalog states: 4-year full-time program (Year 1 courses/clinic at SDSU; Year 2 at UC San Diego; Year 3 SDSU courses + San Diego-area off-campus clinical sites; Year 4 full-time externship). Structure is described only in aggregate as fourteen core courses (seven from each campus) plus fourteen elective courses (minimum four from each campus), ~140 semester-equivalent units; the catalog explicitly notes 'an exact unit minimum is not specified' because it mixes SDSU semester units and UC San Diego quarter units, and it lists no individual course numbers or titles. Degree milestones: maintain 3.0 cumulative GPA in academic and clinical coursework; ~700 hours of precepted clinical experience before the 4th-year externship; pass Year 1 and Year 2 qualifying evaluations; advance to candidacy (prerequisites + Years 1-2 + approved doctoral project); pass a comprehensive examination after Year 3; complete a data-based doctoral project with committee approval and public presentation; full-time 4th-year externship at an approved site. Admits Fall only, no part-time and no transfer students. CAA-accredited. Detailed course lists live on the SDSU program site, not the UCSD catalog.

programs.name: Biology
programs.deptNotes: Combined MS/PhD administrative code for Biology (School of Biological Sciences). No fixed university-published course worksheet is provided because both tracks are research/milestone-based rather than coursework-driven. The PhD is a research doctorate: first-year lab rotations (min. 3), core sequence (e.g., BGGN 208 Grad Launch, BGGN 213 Foundations of Bioinformatics, BGGN 216 Graduate Biostatistics, BGGN 206A/B CORE, BGGN 207 Scientific Ethics), three teaching assistantships, a two-part candidacy exam, and an original dissertation; must advance to candidacy by end of year 4, max 7 years total. The MS is the contiguous BS/MS thesis degree: min. 36 graduate units (200-level), 12 units outside BGGN 271 with no more than 4 upper-division units, six consecutive quarters of research with one mentor, and a defended thesis. Specific coursework is set with the faculty advisor, so no fixed worksheet exists.

programs.name: Biology
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: requirements are milestone-based (first-year laboratory rotations in 3-4 labs, a first-year graduate biology core sequence, three teaching assistantships, a two-part qualifying examination for advancement to candidacy, and original dissertation research), with coursework set by the department/advisor rather than a fixed university-published course list. Named core courses include BGGN 208 (Grad Launch), BGGN 213 (Foundations of Bioinformatics), and BGGN 216 (Graduate Biostatistics). Students must advance to candidacy by the end of year four; total registered time and total support cannot exceed seven years. No fixed course worksheet is published.

The specialization adds distinct elective requirements to the standard doctoral requirements (rotations, core sequence, TAships, candidacy exam, dissertation). NOTE: the department page currently lists the Bioinformatics specialization as 'Currently unavailable, pending curriculum updates,' so no additional specialization course list is published at this time. Bioinformatics remains part of the core via BGGN 213 (Foundations of Bioinformatics).

programs.name: Biology with a Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay (Multiscale Biology) on the base Biology research PhD, so requirements are milestone-based with no fixed university-published course worksheet. It is an interdisciplinary specialization spanning Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, the Jacobs School of Engineering, and Health Sciences, emphasizing a technology-centered hands-on graduate laboratory curriculum and integrative/quantitative analysis across scales from molecule to organism. Students must be admitted to the Biological Sciences PhD and complete all standard doctoral requirements (rotations, core, candidacy exam, dissertation) plus the specialization's interdisciplinary lab curriculum. No fixed course worksheet is published.

programs.name: Biology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay (Anthropogeny) on the base Biology research PhD, so requirements are milestone-based rather than a fixed coursework worksheet. In addition to all standard doctoral requirements, the specialization requires BIOM 225 (Introduction to Anthropogeny) and BIOM 229 (Advanced Anthropogeny) each once (winter/spring of year 2), BIOM 218 (Current Topics in Anthropogeny) for six quarters, participation in monthly research-round seminars, and a dissertation broadly related to and interdisciplinary in human origins. Because the bulk of the degree is dissertation research with advisor-set coursework, no full course worksheet is published.

programs.name: Biology with a Specialization in Quantitative Biology
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay (Quantitative Biology / Q-Bio) on the base Biology research PhD, so requirements are milestone-based with no fixed university-published course worksheet. The specialization, spanning four schools, requires one year of theory courses, a one-year laboratory course sequence during the first two years, and two additional Q-Bio courses, plus first-year lab rotations, on top of all standard doctoral requirements (candidacy exam, dissertation). The catalog states these course categories but not a single fixed enumerated worksheet, and the bulk of the degree is dissertation research; no full course worksheet is published.

Requirements: six consecutive quarters of research with one mentor, a minimum of 36 graduate units (BGGN 200-level or higher) of which 12 must be in courses other than BGGN 271 (with no more than 4 upper-division units), a cumulative and quarterly GPA of 3.0+, three consecutive quarters of graduate residency, and a written thesis with oral defense before a three-member committee. The 12 units of graduate coursework are chosen with the thesis advisor in areas related to the project, so there is no fixed enumerated course list.

programs.name: Biology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay (Interdisciplinary Environmental Research, PIER) on the base Biology research PhD, so requirements are milestone-based with no fixed course worksheet. In addition to completing all standard biology doctoral coursework, dissertation, and requirements, the specialization requires a 16-unit interdisciplinary summer boot camp (SIO 295S-295LS), 8 units from a secondary field outside the home department, 6 units (3 quarters) of the Interdisciplinary Environmental Research Forum (SIO 296), and at least one dissertation chapter broadly related to environmental research. Admission is competitive (roughly 6-8 students/year). Because the bulk of the degree is dissertation research, no full course worksheet is published.

Electives are chosen from an approved set (pick 3), and the degree is dissertation-centered, so no fixed full course worksheet is published.

Students pass seven qualifying exams (Greek and Latin translation, Greek and Roman history, history of Greek and Roman literature, a special-area exam, and an oral exam) before advancing to candidacy, then write and publicly defend a dissertation. Milestones: Second-Year Project, comprehensive/qualifying exams, advancement to candidacy (by end of year five), APA-accredited clinical internship, and dissertation. Joint degree awarded with SDSU; detailed coursework is set by the department/advisor and the SDSU Graduate Bulletin. APA-accredited since 1990.

programs.name: Economics
programs.deptNotes: Research program: requirements are milestone-based (qualifying exams in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics; two fields of specialization; original research paper; advancement to candidacy; dissertation), so no fixed professional course worksheet is published. Concrete facts the catalog does state: PhD first-year core is ECON 200A-C (Microeconomics), 210A-C (Macroeconomics), 220A-C (Econometrics), plus ECON 280 (Computing) and a pre-fall ECON 205 math review; second year adds ECON 220D-F (advanced econometrics) and field electives (minimum seven elective courses, all letter-graded, 3.5+ GPA, across two fields of 2-3 courses each), completed by end of third year; milestone courses include ECON 285 (pre-candidacy presentation), 296 (original research paper), 286 (research workshop). The MA (a research master's, not a terminal professional degree) requires 36 units minimum with a B average in upper-division/doctoral economics courses, at least 24 units from the core first-year sequence (ECON 200, 210, 220), and is qualified for by passing two qualifying exams, or one exam plus a B+ average, or one exam plus a thesis. No foreign language requirement; total registered time cannot exceed seven years. Because the MA is exam/milestone-gated and the code is dominated by the research doctorate, a course worksheet is not appropriate.

programs.name: Economics and International Affairs

The base Economics PhD structure applies (ECON 200/210/220 core sequence plus field electives and dissertation). This is a legacy/administrative ISIS code; the current general catalog Economics graduate page does not publish a separate standalone course list for an 'Economics and International Affairs' track, and the related joint international-affairs doctorate at UCSD is the GPS/Political Science 'Political Science and International Affairs' PhD. No course worksheet is appropriate for a research doctorate of this kind.

Because it is a doctoral specialization on top of a research PhD, no full course worksheet is appropriate.

programs.name: History
programs.deptNotes: No fixed university-published course worksheet applies to this code because it spans a research doctorate plus a faculty-directed MA. The PhD is milestone-based: requirements are set by the field group and advisor (research seminars, historiography courses, cross-field colloquium such as HIGR 200, two minor-field exams, one or two foreign languages depending on field, an oral qualifying exam by the third year, advancement to candidacy by end of year four, and a dissertation) with no single fixed course list — the specific courses differ by concentration (Ancient/East Roman/Post-Roman, East Asian, European, History of Science, Latin American, Middle Eastern, United States). Concrete PhD facts: full-time load 12 units/quarter; ~9 quarters of coursework via Option 1 (two 2-quarter research seminars + three 1-quarter major-field historiography courses + four electives incl. one cross-field colloquium) or Option 2 (three 2-quarter research seminars + three historiography courses + three electives); normative time 7 years (8-year max). The MA is coursework-based (nine four-unit courses = 36 units, all letter-graded, max two upper-division undergrad courses, one-hour oral exam with three examiners over a 40-70 title reading list; no foreign language required) but the specific courses depend on the chosen field concentration (Europe, History of Science, United States, or a faculty-approved Special Field) and are largely selected in consultation with faculty, so no single fixed course list is published. 'MA on the way' is also awarded to continuing PhD students upon passing the qualifying exam.

programs.name: History (Judaic Studies)
programs.deptNotes: No fixed course worksheet is published for this MA concentration. History offers the MA under a set of field concentrations (Europe, History of Science, United States, and faculty-approved Special Fields; the catalog also lists Jewish/Judaic Studies as an available MA area under the auspices of the Department of History). The Judaic/Jewish Studies path is interdisciplinary — students select courses primarily in history and literature but also anthropology, political science, and sociology in consultation with core and affiliated Jewish Studies faculty — so there is no single university-published fixed course/unit list to reproduce. Concrete structure that does apply to the History MA: nine four-unit courses (36 units total), all letter grades, no more than two upper-division undergraduate courses counted, completion in one year full-time or two years part-time, a comprehensive one-hour oral exam before three faculty examiners over a 40-70 title reading list, and no foreign-language requirement. Note: graduate students apply through the Department of History (not directly to the Jewish Studies Program) and work with Jewish Studies core/affiliated faculty; MA admissions in this area are limited/contingent on faculty availability.

programs.name: History (Science Studies)
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: requirements are milestone-based (coursework set by the field group/advisor, minor-field exams, an oral qualifying exam, and a dissertation), so no fixed university-published course worksheet exists. This is the History PhD taken in the History of Science field within the interdisciplinary Science Studies Program (SSP). SSP students major in one of five disciplines (Anthropology, Communication, History, Philosophy, or Sociology) and complete minor-field work in the others; Science Studies is the mandatory minor for History-major SSP students. Concrete facts the pages state: SSP core coursework (Introduction to Science Studies, Advanced Approaches to Science Studies, and two interdisciplinary topical core seminars, plus attendance at the program colloquium; History-side seminars include HIGR 236A-B, 238, 239, 240, 241); most SSP coursework is concentrated in years 1-2, then students deepen disciplinary expertise in History for qualifying exams; competency in one foreign language beyond English is required before advancement to candidacy. General History PhD milestones also apply (full-time 12 units/quarter, two minor-field exams, oral qualifying exam by ~year three, advancement to candidacy by end of year four, dissertation; normative 7-year time-to-degree).

programs.name: History with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate: this is the History PhD (milestone-based — field-group/advisor coursework, two minor-field exams, one or two foreign languages by field, an oral qualifying exam by ~year three, advancement to candidacy by end of year four, and a dissertation, with no fixed university-published course worksheet) plus the interdisciplinary Graduate Specialization in Critical Gender Studies (CGS). The CGS overlay adds five courses beyond the home department's core requirements: CGS 200 (Advanced Studies in Critical Gender Studies, taken shortly after admission), CGS 299 (Practicum in Critical Gender Studies, during the final two years of dissertation writing), and three electives from preapproved seminars in participating departments (or petitioned courses with significant gender/sexuality content). At least one dissertation committee member must be drawn from the CGS core or affiliate faculty. Because the base degree is a research doctorate and this is an add-on specialization, there is no standalone fixed course worksheet.

programs.name: Interdisciplinary Research on Substance Use
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate offered as an SDSU-UC San Diego Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Interdisciplinary Research on Substance Use: requirements are milestone-based, not a fixed UC-San-Diego-published course worksheet. Per the UCSD catalog, students complete a minimum of 60 units total (24 semester units at SDSU in year 1 + 36 quarter units at UC San Diego in year 2), with coursework set jointly by the two campuses/advisor. Advancement to candidacy (required by end of year 3) requires completing coursework and passing a two-part qualifying examination (in-person after year 1; a take-home NIH-style grant proposal after year 2, each requiring at least 80% within two attempts), developing an NIH-style dissertation proposal, and passing an oral defense of that proposal. The dissertation may follow a primary-research or a secondary-research (three sequential first-authored publishable papers) format. Normative time is four years; maximum 6 years registered and 4 years of support. Because coursework is jointly administered with SDSU and driven by milestones/advisor rather than a fixed UCSD course list, no course worksheet is provided.

programs.name: Language and Communicative Disorders

The catalog does state a broad category structure: a Tools requirement (~5 courses: two statistics/research design, one neuroanatomy/physiology, one language structure/theory, one professional survival skills), a Foundations requirement (~5 courses: two normal-language, three disorders-of-language), and an Electives requirement (at least 4 courses, minimum 3 in the chosen concentration) drawn from approved departments (Cognitive Science, Communication, Linguistics, Psychology, Computer Science, Neurosciences). Students choose one of three concentrations (Adult Language, Child Language, or Multilingualism); five-year curriculum; advancement to candidacy by end of year four; max eight years registered time at UC San Diego.

programs.name: Linguistics
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: requirements are milestone-based (comprehensive evaluation, oral qualifying exam, dissertation and public defense) — no fixed university-published unit-summed course worksheet is appropriate. The department does publish a concrete coursework floor: all graduate students take 12 courses before the qualifying exam — 7 required core courses (LIGN 210 Phonetics, LIGN 211 Phonology, LIGN 220 Morphology, LIGN 221 Syntax, LIGN 230 Semantics, LIGN 240 Field Methods, LIGN 293 Research Paper/Practicum) plus 5 electives (>=3 from Linguistics; all letter-graded except LIGN 293). PhD also requires: conversational ability in one non-English language and reading knowledge of a second non-native language; comprehensive evaluation at end of 6th quarter; oral qualifying exam by end of 3rd year; substantial original-research dissertation with public oral defense. The MA (awarded to PhD-track students who complete the 12 courses and pass the comprehensive evaluation) and the CPhil (all PhD requirements except the dissertation) are intermediate/en-route degrees, not terminal professional coursework degrees, so a course worksheet is not provided.

programs.name: Linguistics and Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Joint doctoral / interdisciplinary research PhD: milestone-based (qualifying exam, dissertation, public defense), no fixed university-published course worksheet. Linguistics graduate students are eligible for a joint PhD in Linguistics and Cognitive Science through the Cognitive Science Interdisciplinary PhD Program; most Linguistics faculty hold joint appointments in that program. Joint students satisfy the base Linguistics PhD coursework (7 core LIGN courses + 5 electives, comprehensive evaluation, language requirements, dissertation) and additionally participate in Cognitive Science interdisciplinary requirements including COGS 200 (interdisciplinary seminar) and the COGS 201-series language core (e.g., COGS 201D). Exact interdisciplinary course/unit requirements are set jointly by the two programs and the student's committee rather than as a fixed public worksheet.

programs.name: Linguistics with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Linguistics research PhD, so milestone-based with no fixed worksheet. Students complete ALL standard Linguistics PhD requirements (7 core LIGN courses + 5 electives, comprehensive evaluation, language requirements, qualifying exam, dissertation) PLUS the transdisciplinary Anthropogeny Specialization administered by CARTA: BIOM 225 (Introduction to Anthropogeny, Winter yr 2), BIOM 229 (Advanced Anthropogeny, Spring yr 2), and BIOM 218 (Current Topics in Anthropogeny, taken each quarter for ~4 years), plus monthly research seminars. The dissertation must be broadly related to human origins and interdisciplinary in nature. Because it is a research-doctorate overlay with an advisor/committee-shaped program, no unit-summed course worksheet is published.

programs.name: Linguistics with a Specialization in Computational Social Science
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Linguistics research PhD; milestone-based, no fixed worksheet. Students complete ALL standard Linguistics PhD requirements PLUS the campus Graduate Specialization in Computational Social Science (CSS): three quarters of CSS 209 (Computational Social Science Research Seminar), three graduate courses (at least one outside the home department and at least one 'advanced data' course), at least one CSS-affiliated faculty member from outside Linguistics on the dissertation committee, and a dissertation incorporating a technical/computational social science component. Admission is by application through CSS with endorsement of the primary adviser and department chair. As a research-doctorate overlay, no unit-summed course worksheet is published.

programs.name: Linguistics with a Specialization in Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Linguistics research PhD; milestone-based, no fixed worksheet. Students complete ALL standard Linguistics PhD requirements PLUS the interdepartmental Cognitive Science Specialization (administered through the Cognitive Science Interdisciplinary PhD Program; most Linguistics faculty hold joint appointments). This typically includes participation in the Cognitive Science interdisciplinary seminar (COGS 200) and the COGS 201-series core, with additional requirements set by the Cognitive Science program; the handbook directs students to the Specialization in Cognitive Science site for full details. Because it is a research-doctorate overlay whose exact course set is shaped by the two programs and the student's committee, no unit-summed course worksheet is published.

The MA in Literature is a terminal/embedded master's that does NOT admit independent students - it is awarded to PhD students upon completing qualifying exams. The catalog does state an MA structure of ~48 units: LTTH 210A-B-C (12 units), 24 units in primary/secondary literature concentrations, 4 units elective, and 8 units guided research (298) with a comprehensive examination. Normative time to PhD is six years (max eight).

Coursework shares the same departmental framework as the general Literature PhD (LT77); the embedded terminal MA is awarded only to enrolled PhD students upon qualifying, not to independent MA applicants.

Required core is LTTH 250 + LTTH 255 (8 units) and 20 units of LTWR 215 Cross-Genre Workshop; the remaining units come from literature seminars, art-practice/theory seminars, apprentice teaching, and thesis research (unit ranges below). Additional non-course requirements: two public readings (first-year spring and final quarter), a final manuscript (fiction ~120 pp, poetry ~65 pp, or cross-genre 65-85 pp), and a final thesis committee discussion with four faculty (three from Literature, one external). Full-time status requires 12 units/quarter. The example plan distributes the ranged buckets to sum to 72; actual distribution varies by petition (e.g., TA credit may go up to 24 units and substitute for seminar units).

programs.name: Mathematics with Specialization in Statistics

Concrete facts from the catalog: 72 units required before candidacy, including a 48-unit core curriculum — MATH 280A-B-C (Probability Theory), 281A-B-C (Mathematical Statistics), 282A-B (Applied Statistics), 287A (Time Series), 287B (Multivariate Analysis), 287C (Advanced Time Series), 287D (Statistical Learning). programs.name: Mathematics and Science Education

Concrete facts the official pages state: designed for students holding a master's in biology, chemistry, mathematics, or physics; core coursework includes UC San Diego MSED 296A/296B/296C, MSED 295, MSED 298 and SDSU courses (MSE 603, MSE 801/802/820, plus a science-track TE610C/TE680 or additional math-track courses); three required research-methods courses (SDSU MSE 810 plus a quantitative/qualitative sequence such as UC San Diego PSYC 201A/201B, MATH 282A/282B, or EDS courses). Beyond the core, no fixed number of courses is required; students supplement with electives chosen with their advisor. Milestones: first-year evaluation (~24 units), written and oral comprehensive exams (end of year two), oral dissertation proposal defense (year three), advancement to candidacy by end of year four, and final dissertation defense (five-member committee). Normative time to degree: five years.

programs.name: Music
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: requirements are milestone-based (department/advisor-set coursework by area of emphasis, preliminary exam, qualifying exam with written/oral defense, teaching, and dissertation) with no fixed university-published course worksheet. The Department of Music admits to the doctoral program only; the MA is not a standalone terminal degree but is awarded en route to the PhD for students who have not previously earned a music master's. PhD areas of emphasis are Composition, Computer Music, and Integrative Studies. Core structure stated in the catalog: both methods courses required in the first quarter (MUS 291 Introduction to Research Methods and MUS 501 Introduction to Teaching Methods); minimum 8 units of performance (MUS 200/201/202); minimum 32 units of depth (20 units for the MA); minimum 6 units MUS 298 (pre-qualifying) plus MUS 299 research; 6 units MUS 500 apprentice teaching (three quarters). Advancement requires a preliminary exam (fall of second year), a qualifying exam by end of third year, and a dissertation/major creative work; specific coursework varies by area and advisor, so no single course worksheet applies.

programs.name: Contemporary Music Performance
programs.deptNotes: Performance doctorate (Doctor of Musical Arts in Contemporary Music Performance): requirements are milestone-based rather than a fixed course worksheet. Students complete the shared graduate core (methods courses MUS 291 and MUS 501 in the first quarter; performance and depth unit minimums; apprentice teaching MUS 500), then satisfy a preliminary exam, a qualifying exam, and a recital-based completion requirement. The DMA completion is defined by recitals/projects, not coursework: after the first recital, students give two additional recitals, or one recital plus one of a thesis/research project, an innovative concert or lecture recital, or two approved chamber music concerts. Minimum residence for the DMA is two years. Because progression is exam- and recital-driven with advisor-set coursework, no fixed course worksheet is published.

programs.name: Music and Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Interdisciplinary/specialization research doctorate: this is the Music PhD pursued with an emphasis linking music and cognitive science (integrative/computer-music research), and its requirements are milestone-based rather than a published course worksheet. Cognitive-science and related coursework is taken as advisor-approved depth/electives on top of the standard Music graduate core (methods MUS 291/MUS 501, performance and depth unit minimums, MUS 500 apprentice teaching), followed by preliminary and qualifying exams and a dissertation. No single fixed course list is published because the specific coursework is set by the student's committee and advisor. (Note: the general UCSD Cognitive Science interdisciplinary joint-PhD lists home departments that do not include Music, so this code is administered by the Department of Music.)

Students complete all standard Music PhD requirements (methods MUS 291/MUS 501, performance and depth unit minimums, apprentice teaching, preliminary and qualifying exams, dissertation) AND the CGS specialization: CGS 200 (Advanced Studies in Critical Gender Studies), CGS 299 (Practicum), three electives from preapproved CGS-affiliated seminars, and at least one dissertation-committee member from CGS-affiliated faculty. programs.name: Chemical Engineering with a Specialization in Multiscale Biology
programs.deptNotes: PhD in Chemical Engineering WITH a Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology. Coursework = the standard Chemical Engineering PhD (base code CE75, already worksheeted) PLUS the interdisciplinary Multi-Scale Biology specialization administered by the UCSD Interfaces Graduate Training Program (spanning Jacobs School of Engineering, Health Sciences, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences). Added specialization coursework: complete a minimum of THREE courses total = required BENG 219 (Data Science for Multiscale Biology) PLUS at least two hands-on graduate laboratory courses chosen from the Interfaces list, e.g. BENG 216 (Neuromorphic Integrated Bioelectronics), BENG 277 (Tissue Engineering), BENG/RAD 278 (Medical Imaging Laboratory), BENG 235 (Molecular Imaging and Quantitation in Living Cells), BENG/CHEM/MATH/PHARM 276 (Numerical Analysis for Multiscale Biology), BENG/CHEM 283 (Supramolecular Structure Determination Laboratory), BENG/BGGN 260/PHYS 279 (Multiscale Neurodynamics). Students must satisfy both their home ChemE PhD requirements and the Interfaces specialization requirements. Per-course unit counts not published on the fetched pages, so no full worksheet fabricated.

programs.name: NanoEngineering with a Specialization in Multiscale Biology
programs.deptNotes: PhD in NanoEngineering WITH a Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology. Coursework = the standard NanoEngineering PhD (base code NA75, already worksheeted) PLUS the interdisciplinary Multi-Scale Biology specialization run by the UCSD Interfaces Graduate Training Program (four schools: Jacobs School of Engineering, Health Sciences, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences). Added specialization coursework: complete a minimum of THREE courses total = required BENG 219 (Data Science for Multiscale Biology) PLUS at least two hands-on graduate laboratory courses from the Interfaces list, e.g. BENG 216 (Neuromorphic Integrated Bioelectronics), BENG 277 (Tissue Engineering), BENG/RAD 278 (Medical Imaging Laboratory), BENG 235 (Molecular Imaging and Quantitation in Living Cells), BENG/CHEM/MATH/PHARM 276 (Numerical Analysis for Multiscale Biology), BENG/CHEM 283 (Supramolecular Structure Determination Laboratory), BENG/BGGN 260/PHYS 279 (Multiscale Neurodynamics). Students satisfy both their home NanoEngineering PhD requirements and the Interfaces specialization requirements. programs.name: Neurosciences
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: the Neurosciences Graduate Program (NGP) admits students only for the PhD and does not offer a standalone/terminal coursework Master's (an MS may be conferred only en route). Requirements are milestone-based — a set of mandatory core courses plus advisor-guided electives, first-year research rotations, an ethics course, a teaching assistantship (minimum one quarter), a qualifying exam / advancement to candidacy (targeted by end of year 3-4), and a doctoral dissertation defense — so no fixed university-published course worksheet with unit totals exists. Concrete facts the department states: mandatory core coursework centers on NEU 200A-B-C (Basic Neuroscience) plus additional core courses (e.g., statistics/experimental design, neuroanatomy lab, minor proposition), with core electives such as NEU 221 (Advanced Topics), NEU 231 (Tools for Experimental Data Analysis), NEU 265 (Mechanisms of Pain), and NEU 270A/270B (Neurobiology of Disease). Time to degree is normally under 6 years (max support 6 years, max registered time 7 years). Verify current core-course list and units with the NGP Student Handbook.

programs.name: Neurosciences and Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate (interdisciplinary Neurosciences and Cognitive Science track): as with all NGP PhDs, requirements are milestone-based — mandatory neuroscience core coursework, advisor-guided electives, research rotations, teaching, a qualifying exam / advancement to candidacy, and a dissertation defense — combined with cognitive-science-oriented coursework. No fixed university-published course worksheet with unit totals is defined; the specific course set is set by the department and the student's advisory committee. Base PhD facts are as for NE75 (NEU 200A-B-C core plus additional core and electives; ~under 6 years to degree). Confirm the exact combined-track course expectations with the NGP Student Handbook and the Cognitive Science graduate office.

programs.name: Neurosciences with a Specialization in Computational Neurosciences
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the research-doctorate Neurosciences PhD (base = NE75), so it is milestone-based with no fixed standalone worksheet: students complete all base NGP PhD requirements (core coursework, rotations, teaching, qualifying exam/advancement, dissertation) PLUS the Computational Neuroscience Specialization (CNS). CNS adds four approved computational-neuroscience courses beyond the departmental PhD requirements (typically taken in years 2-3), e.g. Neurodynamics (BGGN 260), Neurophysics of brain circuits and networks (PHYS 278), Probability and statistics for data science (DSC 212), plus one additional approved course; for NGP students the CNS waives one statistics requirement. Students must also participate in and present at a weekly neuro-theory journal club. Math prerequisites: calculus, ODEs, linear algebra, probability (MATLAB/Python recommended). The diploma notes the parent PhD plus 'Specialization in Computational Neuroscience.' No terminal coursework MS is published; verify the current approved course list in the NGP Handbook.

programs.name: Neurosciences with a Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay ('with a Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology') on the research-doctorate Neurosciences PhD, so requirements are milestone-based: students complete all base NGP PhD requirements (core coursework, research rotations, teaching, qualifying exam/advancement to candidacy, dissertation) plus the additional Multi-Scale Biology specialization coursework/training. No fixed university-published course worksheet with unit totals is defined; the specialization course set is administered by the interdisciplinary training program and the student's advisor. The specific approved course list for this specialization was not found on the fetched official pages — confirm with the NGP Student Handbook / the Multi-Scale Biology training program.

programs.name: Neurosciences with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
programs.deptNotes: Transdisciplinary specialization overlay ('with a Specialization in Anthropogeny', administered by CARTA) on the research-doctorate Neurosciences PhD, so requirements are milestone-based: students complete all base NGP PhD requirements (core coursework, rotations, teaching, qualifying exam/advancement, dissertation) plus the CARTA Anthropogeny specialization track (transdisciplinary coursework/seminars on the origins of the human phenomenon spanning the social and natural sciences). No fixed university-published course worksheet with unit totals exists for the specialization; the track is defined and administered by CARTA together with the student's advisor. Confirm current specialization requirements on the CARTA specialization-track page and the NGP Handbook.

programs.name: Neurosciences with a Specialization in Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Interdisciplinary specialization overlay ('with a Specialization in Cognitive Science', the Specialization in Cognitive Science / SCS administered by the Department of Psychology) on the research-doctorate Neurosciences PhD, so requirements are milestone-based: students complete all base NGP PhD requirements (core coursework, rotations, teaching, qualifying exam/advancement, dissertation) plus the SCS specialization coursework and seminar. The SCS is open to doctoral students in participating departments (including Neuroscience); students apply through the SCS administration with the endorsement of their research adviser and department chair. No fixed university-published course worksheet with unit totals is defined for the specialization; confirm current requirements on the Psychology interdisciplinary-programs page and the NGP Handbook.

programs.name: Philosophy
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate with an MA available only en route: requirements are milestone-based (coursework set by the department/advisor, qualifying paper, candidacy exam, teaching, dissertation), so no fixed university-published course worksheet exists. The department does NOT admit terminal master's students; the MA is earned in the course of PhD progress. Concrete facts the catalog states: over the first two years students take at least 3 courses/quarter (at least 2 philosophy seminars, PHIL 200-285); a required fall Proseminar in year 1; 14 total graduate seminars (12 in philosophy) with B+ or better before candidacy; a 9-seminar distribution across 5 areas (history incl. one ancient + one modern, philosophy of science, mind/language, ethics/political, metaphysics/epistemology); logic proficiency in predicate calculus (exam or PHIL 120, B+) in year 1 and an advanced logic/formal-methods course (PHIL 122, 123, or 125) with B+ by year 2; a 7,500-9,000 word third-year qualifying paper; a research-skills requirement; TA service for at least 3 quarters; advancement to candidacy by end of year 4; dissertation with oral defense (normative time 6 years). MA en route requires 8 distribution seminars (no more than 4 from any one area) plus a master's research paper approved by two faculty. The MA/CPH/PHD codes are administrative variants of the same milestone-based program, not separate coursework worksheets.

programs.name: Philosophy (Science Studies)
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate (interdisciplinary Science Studies Program), so requirements are milestone-based with no fixed university-published course worksheet: students complete all standard Philosophy PhD requirements PLUS the Science Studies amendments. Concrete facts the catalog states: attend the Science Studies Colloquium in years 1 and 2, receiving PHIL 209C credit (S/U) in two quarters; before the prospectus defense complete PHIL 209A (Introduction to Science Studies I), PHIL 209D (Introduction to Science Studies II), and two iterations of PHIL 209B (Core Seminar in Science Studies); two additional science-studies courses outside philosophy from an approved list (one science course may substitute for one); an amended distribution (at least one seminar from each of the five areas and at least two from any four areas); and a dissertation committee that includes one core Science Studies Program faculty member. Because the base is a milestone-based doctorate, a full course worksheet is not appropriate.

programs.name: Philosophy and Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate combining Philosophy with Cognitive Science: requirements are milestone-based (coursework, qualifying/candidacy exams, teaching, dissertation coordinated across the two fields), so no fixed university-published course worksheet exists. It builds on the standard Philosophy PhD (fall Proseminar; 14 graduate seminars/12 in philosophy at B+; 9-seminar distribution across 5 areas; logic proficiency via PHIL 120 and an advanced logic course PHIL 122/123/125; third-year qualifying paper; 3 quarters TA; candidacy by year 4; dissertation) with cognitive-science coursework and committee involvement determined by the department/advisor. Course lists are not fixed at the university level, so overview rather than a worksheet.

programs.name: Philosophy with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate (Program in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research, PIER), so requirements are milestone-based with no fixed university-published course worksheet: students complete ALL standard Philosophy PhD requirements PLUS the PIER additions. Concrete facts the catalog states: a 16-unit interdisciplinary summer boot camp (SIO 295S / 295LS); 8 units of coursework in a secondary field outside philosophy; 6 units (three quarters) of the Interdisciplinary Environmental Research Forum (SIO 296); and at least one dissertation chapter on environmental research using an interdisciplinary approach. Admission is competitive (roughly 6-8 students/year across ~10 departments), typically begun in the third year after core coursework. Because the base is a milestone-based doctorate plus an overlay, a full course worksheet is not appropriate.

programs.name: Philosophy with a Specialization in Cognitive Science
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate (Specialization in Cognitive Science, SCS, administered through the Cognitive Science program), so requirements are milestone-based with no fixed university-published course worksheet: students complete all standard Philosophy PhD requirements PLUS the SCS requirements. The specialization is open to PhD students in several departments (including philosophy) and may be added anytime precandidacy. Because the base is a milestone-based doctorate plus an overlay, a full course worksheet is not appropriate.

programs.name: Physics (Biophysics)
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate (Physics PhD, Biophysics track): requirements are milestone-based (coursework set by the department/advisor, qualifying/candidacy examination, teaching requirement, and dissertation defense); no fixed university-published course worksheet exists. An MS may be earned en route under Plan I (thesis) or Plan II (comprehensive exam).

programs.name: Physics
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate (main Physics PhD; the MS is a research degree, not a professional coursework program): requirements are milestone-based (advisor-directed coursework, qualifying/candidacy examination, teaching, and dissertation), so no fixed course worksheet is published. There is no standalone MS — a master's is earned only en route to or in place of the PhD under Plan I (master's thesis) or Plan II (comprehensive oral examination), so there is no set coursework worksheet for the MS either. Stated requirements: seven core courses with B or better (PHYS 200A, 201, 203A-B, 210A, 212A-B), typically completed in year one (two-year maximum); three advanced graduate courses drawn from at least two of eight groups (Plasma, Condensed Matter, Particle/High-Energy, Mathematics, Biophysics, Astrophysics, General, Computational) with B or better by end of year three; PhD candidacy exam; teaching requirement; and thesis defense.

programs.name: Physics with Specialization in Material Physics
programs.deptNotes: Research (thesis) master's, not a professional coursework program: the MS in Physics with a specialization in Materials Physics is a Plan I (thesis) program only and, per the department, is open only to UC San Diego undergraduates. Because completion is defined by advisor-supervised research and a master's thesis rather than a fixed university-published course list, no course worksheet is appropriate. The physics graduate coursework framework (seven core courses; advanced graduate courses grouped by area, including a Condensed Matter group relevant to materials physics) applies as background, but no fixed unit/course worksheet is published for this MS.

programs.name: Physics with Specialization in Bioinformatics
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate: this is the Physics PhD with the interdisciplinary Specialization in Bioinformatics (administered through the campus-wide Bioinformatics and Systems Biology program, which draws faculty from Biological Sciences, Bioengineering, Chemistry/Biochemistry, CSE, Mathematics, Physics, and Biomedical Sciences). Requirements = the base Physics PhD (milestone-based: core courses, candidacy exam, teaching, dissertation) plus additional bioinformatics coursework specified by the interdisciplinary program and the student's advisor. No single fixed university-published course worksheet defines this overlay, so an overview is provided rather than a worksheet.

programs.name: Physics with a Specialization in Computational Science
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate: Physics PhD with the interdisciplinary Specialization in Computational Science (the CSME / Computational Science, Mathematics, and Engineering program, integrated across seven participating departments). Requirements = the base Physics PhD (milestone-based: core courses, candidacy exam, teaching, dissertation) plus the specialization's additional requirements (per the department page, additional qualifying-exam and elective coursework in computational science). No fixed university-published course worksheet defines the overlay, so an overview is given.

programs.name: Physics with Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on a research doctorate: Physics PhD with the interdisciplinary Ph.D. Specialization in Multi-Scale Biology (introduced Spring 2009, spanning Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, Jacobs School of Engineering, and Health Sciences). The specialization adds coursework (BENG 219 Data Science for Multiscale Biology plus at least two additional hands-on interdisciplinary graduate laboratory courses, for at least three courses total) on top of the base Physics PhD, whose requirements are milestone-based (core courses, candidacy exam, teaching, dissertation). No single fixed university-published worksheet combines the base degree and overlay, so an overview is provided.

programs.name: Physics with a Specialization in Quantitative Biology

It adds theory and laboratory coursework over roughly two years on top of the base Physics PhD, whose requirements are milestone-based (core courses, candidacy exam, teaching, dissertation). No fixed university-published course worksheet defines the overlay, so an overview is provided.

programs.name: Physics with a Specialization in Computational Neuroscience

Per the department page it adds three specialization core courses on top of the base Physics PhD, whose requirements are milestone-based (core courses, candidacy exam, teaching, dissertation). No fixed university-published course worksheet defines the overlay, so an overview is provided.

programs.name: Political Science
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate (plus a research/qualifying MA): requirements are milestone-based (coursework set by the department/advisor, qualifying exam papers, dissertation), so no fixed university-published course worksheet applies. PhD facts stated on the official page: 18 quarter courses by end of Year 2 with GPA >= 3.3; mandatory four-course core POLI 203A-B and 204A-B (no substitutions); at least 15 of the 18 courses numbered POLI 200-279; max 3 S/U courses; up to 4 courses of transfer credit with department permission; 9 courses done by end of Year 1. Qualifying exam by end of Year 2 in two fields chosen from American politics, comparative politics, international relations, methodology, political theory, with a solo-authored research paper (<=10,000 words) and review paper (<=8,000 words). Year 3 workshop enrollment (POLI 280-289) with a prospectus/research presentation; advancement to candidacy via prospectus defense by end of fall Year 4; dissertation completion targeted by end of Year 6. The MA is milestone-based: 15 quarter courses (9 letter-graded, numbered POLI 200-279) plus one department-approved seminar paper. Reference only; confirm with the department.

programs.name: Political Science and International Affairs
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate offered jointly by the Department of Political Science and the School of Global Policy and Strategy (GPS): requirements are milestone-based (qualifying exams, prospectus/advancement, dissertation), so no fixed university-published course worksheet applies. Official facts: 18 courses required prior to advancement to candidacy by end of Year 2, including the common four-course core POLI 203A-B and 204A-B (no substitutions); required first-year curriculum in politics and research methods; second-year coursework focused on the chosen research area. Each student is assigned a faculty adviser in GPS and must select a departmental prospectus adviser by the start of Year 3. Regional-language fluency is expected for comparative-politics/policy field specialization and language training may be credited. Reference only; confirm with the department/GPS.

programs.name: Political Science with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the Political Science research doctorate: base PhD requirements (milestone-based: 18 courses incl. core POLI 203A-B/204A-B, qualifying exams, dissertation) plus the Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) overlay, so no fixed course worksheet applies. Overlay facts from the official page: complete all standard Political Science PhD requirements PLUS a 16-unit interdisciplinary summer boot camp (SIO 295S-295LS), 8 units from a secondary field outside the department, and 6 units (three quarters) of the Interdisciplinary Environmental Research Forum (SIO 296); at least one dissertation chapter must be broadly related to, and interdisciplinary in nature regarding, environmental research. Admission is competitive (roughly six to eight students admitted annually across participating departments). Reference only; confirm with the department.

programs.name: Political Science and International Affairs with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
programs.deptNotes: Specialization overlay on the joint Political Science and International Affairs research doctorate (Political Science + GPS): base joint-PhD requirements are milestone-based (18 courses incl. core POLI 203A-B/204A-B, qualifying exams, prospectus, dissertation) plus the Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) overlay, so no fixed course worksheet applies. Overlay facts from the official page: complete all political science and international affairs PhD requirements PLUS a 16-unit interdisciplinary summer boot camp (SIO 295S-295LS), 8 units from a secondary field outside the home department, and 6 units (three quarters) of interdisciplinary environmental research work (SIO 296); at least one dissertation chapter is broadly related to and interdisciplinary in environmental research. Reference only; confirm with the department/GPS.

programs.name: Political Science with a Specialization in Computational Social Science

Overlay facts from the official page: in addition to all PhD requirements, complete three quarters of CSS 209 (research seminar) and three electives (at least one outside the home department and at least one from designated advanced-data courses); at least one dissertation committee member must be a CSS-affiliated faculty member not affiliated with the student's home department; the dissertation must include a technical and/or computational social science component. Reference only; confirm with the department.

Total university support may not exceed eight years. The MA in Experimental Psychology requires the first-year courses, three area proseminars, and graduate unit minimums (at least 14 units in graduate courses in the major field, 10 additional graduate units, and 12 units in graduate or upper-division courses). Exact seminar selections are chosen with the adviser, so no single fixed course worksheet is published.

programs.name: Experimental Psychology & Cognitive Science

Specific courses are chosen with the adviser, so no fixed worksheet is published.

Concrete facts from the official page: 72 units total (~18 courses); required core includes VIS 200 (Methods and Theories) or VIS 204 (Rethinking Art History), plus VIS 500 and VIS 502; four breadth courses from distinct areas (e.g., Medieval/Renaissance/Early Modern, Modern/Contemporary, Media Studies, Meso-American/North American Indigenous, Asian, Latin American, Material Culture, Design Studies); minimum six art-history seminars among electives; competency in TWO languages other than English before advancing to candidacy; a year-three qualifying exam (two bibliographies, qualifying paper, dissertation prospectus, a five-day/two-essay written exam, and a 2-2.5 hour oral exam); and a dissertation with oral defense. The MA is a degree awarded to PhD students who meet completion standards (12 four-unit courses, a written field exam, a language exam, and an MA thesis), not a separately admitted terminal program.

programs.name: Art History, Theory, and Criticism with a Concentration in Art Practice
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate: requirements are milestone-based (individualized coursework with the advisor, qualifying examination, apprentice teaching, language competency, and a dissertation) with no fixed university-published course worksheet. This is the Art Practice concentration of the VA76 doctorate, for artists engaged in advanced research. Concrete facts from the official page: 72 units total (~18 courses); required core includes VIS 200 or VIS 204, VIS 206 (Seminar in Art Practice Research), VIS 207 (working practice, repeated), one VIS 210-219 art theory/practice seminar, plus VIS 500 and VIS 502; three breadth courses from distinct areas; minimum three art-history seminars among electives; competency in ONE language other than English before advancing to candidacy; a year-three qualifying exam (slightly expanded vs. VA76); and a dissertation that additionally includes produced/exhibited studio, media, or performance work with an oral defense.

programs.name: Art, Theory, and Criticism with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
programs.deptNotes: Research doctorate with a specialization overlay: this is the VA76 Art History, Theory, and Criticism PhD plus the interdisciplinary Specialization in Anthropogeny. Requirements are milestone-based (base PhD coursework, qualifying exam, language competency, dissertation) with no fixed university-published course worksheet. The Anthropogeny specialization adds extra coursework beyond the PhD requirements: an introduction and advanced anthropogeny course, regular attendance at the Current Topics in Anthropogeny seminar over ~4 years, monthly research seminars, and a dissertation broadly related to human origins. Base PhD facts: 72 units total, two-language competency before candidacy, year-three qualifying exam, and a dissertation defense (see VA76).
